name: CORTEX
concept: Autonomous vulnerability-triage and exploit-orchestration decision engine: it ingests cheap probes (banners, HTTP behavior, TLS metadata, response differentials), scores candidate vulnerabilities from a plug-in registry against likelihood x impact with per-attempt cost, ranks and executes exploit plug-ins by priority with outcome feedback that re-ranks survivors, and emits a red-team report synthesizing evidence (request/response pairs, timings, exit codes) for every attempted path. The meta-brain and report generator are the deliverable; exploit coverage is declarative, precondition-declaring plug-ins kept lab-safe.
attack_vectors: service banner/version fingerprinting -> CVE plug-in match
HTTP response-behavior differentials -> web plug-in selection
TLS certificate metadata -> exact-version pinning before firing
recursive post-attempt re-ranking (prune dead paths, promote survivors, refund attempt budget)
precondition-confidence gating: probe verifies reachability before a high-impact plug-in launches
novelty_angle: Unlike fire-everything autopwn engines, this is an explicit decision-theoretic triage brain with outcome-feedback loops and evidence-preserving report synthesis — exploits are inert declarative plug-ins (preconditions/trust/lab-safety flags) so the orchestrator grows coverage without touching the planner, and what worked/failed becomes training signal for the next iteration.
dependencies: Python stdlib only: socket, ssl, http.client, urllib, json, subprocess, time, re
json/YAML plug-in manifest registry (preconditions, confidence, impact, attempt cost, lab-safety flag)
harmless lab payload templates under tool/payloads/
scope_gate: Every socket/packet funneled through a single scope-checked dial wrapper that resolves and CIDR-validates target against state/allow.conf (loopback + RFC1918 + user-supplied lab CIDR) BEFORE any byte leaves the box; plug-in blocked if its declared preconditions reference out-of-allowlist addresses; first run prints WARN banner and refuses with non-zero exit on any out-of-scope target; re-asserted per attempt so scope cannot drift.
